lines.trans: After running a full witch hunt and tearing me to shreds, why do people keep calling my phone?!
Hey Joon-mo, ugh, traffic is completely jammed—did you finish meeting the park rep?
Finished ages ago—hey, by the time you get here this park is going to close!
They say fireworks are one hour away—hurry over!
Wait no—do not speed or overtake cars out of temper just because I said that; drive carefully!
Yeah, I will call once I get there.
Right—now where did Cindy and Seung-chan go?
Anyone watching would think I just got rejected by a guy—I have not even heard his answer yet!
His heart must have raced too—since a celebrity kissed him out of nowhere, he must have been totally stunned.

examples.trans: Yeah, wait—why are you suddenly calling me plain Senior? Where did the honorific suffix go?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.
I want to got turned down! right now.
How about trying to got turned down! together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
Money is left.
Time is left.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

examples.text: 병원 문 닫고 네 매형 백수 되게 생겼다니까.
examples.trans: The clinic is about to close and turn your brother-in-law into an unemployed man.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 닫다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (close and).

examples.text: 어 준모야, 아유 차가 너무 막혀. 너 담당자랑 미팅은 다 했어?
examples.trans: Hey Joon-mo, ugh, traffic is completely jammed—did you finish meeting the park rep?
This point about with the person in charge is really important.
Cindy, panic written all over her face!
This expression comes from 'flustered, panicked'.

examples.text: 뭐야, 왜 대답을 못 해? 갑자기 왜 선배님이 선배가 됐지?
examples.trans: What is it, why can you not answer? How did honored Senior suddenly turn into plain Senior?

examples.text: 당연하지, 좋지! 우리 술 먹을 때 원래 이러고 놀아, 무조건 대답을 당연하지라고 해야 되는 거야.
examples.trans: Of course, I love it! We always play this when drinking—no matter what, you have to answer "Of course"!

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).
Listen well.
Listen to a song.

examples.text: 아 미치겠네, 이거 봐 손 떨리는 거!
examples.trans: Oh man, look at my hands shaking right here!

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.

examples.text: 아주 마녀사냥을 해서 사람을 묵사발을 만들어놓고 왜 자꾸 전화를 해!
examples.trans: After running a full witch hunt and tearing me to shreds, why do people keep calling my phone?!
This point about a witch hunt is really important.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

examples.text: 내가 편집을 기가 막히게 해서 그렇지, 쟤가 무슨 남자야, 애지!
examples.trans: Only because my editing is phenomenal—what kind of grown man is he, he is just a kid!
This expression comes from 'breathtakingly, brilliantly'.

examples.text: 아주 마녀사냥을 해서 사람을 묵사발을 만들어놓고 왜 자꾸 전화를 해!
examples.trans: After running a full witch hunt and tearing me to shreds, why do people keep calling my phone?!
Let us do that (turning into and) right away.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

examples.text: 아주 마녀사냥을 해서 사람을 묵사발을 만들어놓고 왜 자꾸 전화를 해!
examples.trans: After running a full witch hunt and tearing me to shreds, why do people keep calling my phone?!

meanings.note: Used for room doors, building entrances, and car doors

examples.trans: It's cold, so please close the door.

examples.text: 차 문을 열 때 옆 차를 조심하세요.
examples.trans: Watch out for the next car when opening your car door.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.

examples.text: 아이고, 얘는 온다 온다 하고 왜 이렇게 안 와? 불꽃놀이 그렇게 좋아하면서 20분밖에 안 남았구먼!
examples.trans: Good grief, she keeps saying she is coming—why is she still not here when fireworks start in twenty minutes?!

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.
Where is my handbag?

examples.text: 글쎄 그게 무슨 또라이 같은 소리냐고! 박 군은 어딨니?

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.

Why are you running?

examples.text: 자꾸 어디 넘어지고 또 칠칠맞게 뭐 하다 다쳤냐?

meanings.note: The person called is marked with 에게 or 한테 (e.g., 친구한테 전화하다).

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.

meanings.note: Used to warn or advise caution.

examples.trans: Please be careful.
Please be careful. (2)

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?
Did you hear about this since?
I was busy today because of since.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.

examples.text: 어 아니 아니, 그렇다고 막 속도 내고 승질 난다고 추월하고 그러지 말고 조심해서 와!
examples.trans: Wait no—do not speed or overtake cars out of temper just because I said that; drive carefully!

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
